skill.name: set-up-cloudflare-meta-new-customer-bidding
skill.description: Review Meta conversion tracking for a Cloudflare storefront through Product Metrics. Cloudflare Tracking alone cannot verify first-time buyers, so the guide explains supported bidding alternatives and when backend order history is needed.
skill.summary: Check Meta conversion tracking and determine whether your storefront can support bidding for new customers.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are documentation, scoped setup checks, or references, not reconnaissance or backtick execution. Confirmed risks include unpinned installation, blanket permission approval, customer order access, and authenticated writes without a general approval step. The skill also solicits sensitive credentials, trusts external instructions and browser links without verification, and contradicts its own guidance on first-time buyers.

remediation.issue: The agent is allowed to solicit and pass sensitive credentials to commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to enter the Meta token in the verified Product Metrics app. Remove credential requests from agent instructions, including exceptions for unrelated platforms.

remediation.issue: Cloudflare troubleshooting tells users to approve every permission.
remediation.suggestion: List the minimum required permissions and their purpose. Ask an administrator to verify the exact account, zone, and grants before continuing.

remediation.issue: The workflow does not require approval for all authenticated setup writes.
remediation.suggestion: Preview the proposed changes and confirm the workspace, property, and Meta destination before writing. Verify consent settings before enabling event delivery.

remediation.issue: The workflow can retrieve more order data than the classification task needs.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the workspace and storefront before reading orders. Limit retrieval to required fields and report aggregate classifications without shopper details.

remediation.issue: Remote documentation and tool-returned browser links cross trust boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: Use bundled or pinned references and treat external content as data. Verify browser links against expected origins and redirect destinations before presenting them.

remediation.issue: The installer command does not pin the package version or source revision.
remediation.suggestion: Publish installation instructions with a reviewed installer version and an immutable skill revision. Keep installation separate from the setup workflow and require explicit approval.

remediation.issue: The description promises a new-customer signal that Cloudflare Tracking alone does not emit.
remediation.suggestion: Correct the source description and make order-history verification a prerequisite. Explain that revenue, profit, and returning-customer signals are not substitutes for first-time buyer identification.

semantic_findings.title: New-Customer Bidding Claim Conflicts With the Data Source
semantic_findings.description: The description promises first-order conversion events, but the guide says Cloudflare Tracking cannot verify a first order. Merchants could enable tracking or select a paid campaign objective expecting a signal that never arrives.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reference explicitly says neither first-order event is sent for Cloudflare-only orders. The source description explicitly promises a separate first-order conversion.

semantic_findings.title: Live Documentation Can Replace Reviewed Instructions

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback explicitly substitutes unpinned live documentation for local guides. No evidence found of malicious content in the bundled guides.

semantic_findings.title: Browser Handoff Does Not Validate the Destination

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The handoff rule accepts the returned URL without a documented origin check. No evidence found of an actual malicious URL.

content.user_title: Assess Meta New-Customer Bidding with Cloudflare
content.value_statement: A Cloudflare order confirmation page cannot show whether a buyer has purchased before. This guide helps you check Meta event delivery, compare bidding alternatives, and identify when you need backend order history.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status through its CLI or MCP and identify incomplete connection steps.
Guide a workspace administrator through connecting a proxied Cloudflare storefront to a Product Metrics property.
Guide a user through connecting a Meta pixel or dataset and checking test event delivery.
Review scoped order records to distinguish observed returning buyers from buyers whose status is unknown.
Explain profit and returning-customer bidding alternatives and when a signed backend order feed can provide missing history.
limitations: Cloudflare Tracking alone does not emit new-customer revenue or profit events because the confirmation page lacks purchase history.
Returning-customer classification is limited to identified buyers with prior paid orders observed since tracking went live.
Profit events require enough cost data to calculate margin, including fallback product costs and other costs for Cloudflare orders.
Users must complete Cloudflare authorization and select campaign optimization events in Meta themselves.

use_cases.title: Check acquisition tracking before connecting
use_cases.description: Find out if your Cloudflare storefront can supply a first-time buyer signal before connecting accounts.

use_cases.title: Investigate missing Meta conversions
use_cases.description: Separate a missing first-order signal from a delivery, consent, or test configuration problem.

use_cases.title: Scope a backend order integration
use_cases.description: Identify what paid order history the backend must provide to distinguish new buyers from returning ones.

prompt_templates.title: Check first-time buyer support
prompt_templates.prompt: My store only uses Cloudflare Tracking. Can Meta receive a verified first-time buyer event? Explain the limitation without connecting any accounts.

prompt_templates.title: Review the current setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the Cloudflare and Meta connection status for my storefront. Confirm the workspace and property first. Do not change any settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic diagnostic: review a connected storefront.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a missing conversion
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me interpret a Meta test order that appears as a purchase but not as a new-customer conversion. Check consent and tracking status without changing settings. Summarize available bidding alternatives.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: distinguish delivery issues from unsupported events.

prompt_templates.title: Plan reliable first-order classification
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a plan for a signed backend order integration that includes customer order history. Explain how Cloudflare Tracking still links visits to orders. Propose validation checks without deploying anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: plan an integration for verified first-time buyers.

output_examples.input: Meta received my test purchase. Why is there no new-customer event?
output_examples.output: The test purchase confirms delivery, not first-time buyer status. Cloudflare Tracking reads the confirmation page, which does not include prior purchases. No new-customer event is expected.

output_examples.input: What can I optimize for if I only use Cloudflare Tracking?
output_examples.output: Use all-order profit when margin data is complete, or returning-customer events for identified buyers with a prior tracked purchase. Neither option identifies first-time buyers.

output_examples.input: What do I need to verify a buyer's first order?
output_examples.output: Have a developer send signed backend order updates with customer order history. Keep Cloudflare Tracking to link visits to orders.

best_practices: Confirm the storefront, property, and Meta dataset before reviewing events or approving any setup change.
Enter access tokens in the verified Product Metrics app, not in chat or tool arguments.
Verify consent settings and delivery with a test order. Remove the test event code before relying on production reporting.
anti_patterns: Treating a buyer's first tracked purchase as proof that they have never purchased before.
Selecting a new-customer optimization event before confirming that the data source can send it.
Approving Cloudflare permissions without reviewing the requesting app, selected zone, and requested access.

faq.question: Can Cloudflare Tracking alone send new-customer events to Meta?
faq.answer: No. The order confirmation page does not provide purchase history, so Product Metrics cannot verify that a purchase is the customer's first.

faq.question: Do purchases still reach Meta?
faq.answer: Yes, through the Meta Conversions API when the destination is active and consent permits. Profit events also require complete margin data.

faq.question: Can it recognize buyers from before tracking went live?
faq.answer: Not from Cloudflare Tracking alone. Returning status requires an identified buyer whose previous paid order Product Metrics has already observed.

faq.question: How can I add the missing order history?
faq.answer: A developer can send signed backend order updates with customer order history through the Custom Store or webhook integration.

faq.question: Can I optimize for profit without item-level costs?
faq.answer: Yes. Product Metrics uses your fallback product cost percentage and additional costs to calculate margin for Cloudflare orders.

faq.question: Who selects the campaign optimization event?
faq.answer: You select the event in Meta. The skill can explain the steps, but the choice stays with you.
